topicName: Tree-Based Models (Decision Trees, Random Forests, Gradient Boosting)
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Tree-Based Models: Decision Trees, Random Forests, and Gradient Boosting"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Tree-based models are foundational algorithms in machine learning, widely used for both classification and regression tasks. They are intuitive, highly interpretable, and form the basis of some of the most powerful predictive engines in data science."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Decision Trees"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"A Decision Tree splits the data into subsets based on feature value thresholds. It recursively partitions the feature space until a stopping criterion is met, such as maximum depth or minimum samples per leaf."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Gini Impurity and Entropy are the primary metrics used to determine the quality of a split."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Pros: Easy to understand, requires little data preprocessing, handles both numerical and categorical data."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Cons: Prone to overfitting, especially when trees grow very deep without regularization."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"from sklearn.tree import DecisionTreeClassifier
from sklearn.datasets import load_iris
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split

data = load_iris()
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(data.data, data.target, test_size=0.2, random_state=42)
clf = DecisionTreeClassifier(max_depth=3, random_state=42)
clf.fit(X_train, y_train)
print('Accuracy:', clf.score(X_test, y_test))"},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Random Forests"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Random Forest is an ensemble learning method that constructs a multitude of decision trees during training and outputs the mode of the classes (classification) or mean prediction (regression) of the individual trees."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Bootstrap Aggregating (Bagging): Each tree is trained on a random subset of the data with replacement."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Feature Randomness: At each split, only a random subset of features is considered, reducing correlation between trees."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier

rf = RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=100, random_state=42)
rf.fit(X_train, y_train)
print('Random Forest Accuracy:', rf.score(X_test, y_test))"},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Gradient Boosting"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"Gradient Boosting builds trees sequentially, where each new tree attempts to correct the errors (residuals) made by the previous sequence of trees. Popular implementations include XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Boosting focuses on reducing bias, whereas Bagging focuses on reducing variance."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Requires careful tuning of hyperparameters such as learning rate (shrinkage) and number of estimators."},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"from sklearn.ensemble import GradientBoostingClassifier

gbc = GradientBoostingClassifier(n_estimators=100, learning_rate=0.1, random_state=42)
gbc.fit(X_train, y_train)
print('Gradient Boosting Accuracy:', gbc.score(X_test, y_test))"},{"order":19,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"Start with a simple Decision Tree as a baseline, scale up to Random Forests for robust, out-of-the-box performance, and employ Gradient Boosting when maximizing predictive accuracy is the primary goal."}]
